name: ESSAI 2026
venue: European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence, Vienna, Austria
description: The 2026 European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence (ESSAI) is a one‑week program for PhD students, young researchers and senior scholars. It offers introductory and advanced courses across all AI sub‑disciplines, with special thematic tracks on Bilateral AI and Digital Humanism, as well as invited tutorials and networking opportunities. The school also includes a rich social programme, such as a reception at Vienna City Hall, to foster community building among participants.

name: OpenEuroLLM Winter School
venue: Skeikampen conference hotel, near Oslo, Norway
description: The 2026 Winter School on Multilinguality in LLM Development and Evaluation is organized by the Nordic Language Processing Laboratory in collaboration with the OpenEuroLLM project. It targets NLP researchers, especially those from EuroHPC consortium countries and doctoral students, and focuses on multilingual large language models, their evaluation, data curation, and dialectal challenges. The event takes place at the Skeikampen conference hotel north of Oslo, offering a mountain setting with ski and walking opportunities, and includes subsidized participation and group bus transfers.

name: Probabilistic AI School
description: The ProbAI School 2026 is a Probabilistic AI School taking place in Vilnius, Lithuania. It aims to provide an inclusive educational environment covering state‑of‑the‑art machine learning and artificial intelligence topics for students, academics and industry professionals. The five‑day program runs from 3 to 7 August 2026 and is co‑organized with the Artificial Intelligence Association of Lithuania.

name: BMVA Computer Vision Summer School
description: The 29th BMVA Computer Vision Summer School will be held at Durham University in Durham, England, UK. It offers an intensive week of lectures and lab sessions covering a broad spectrum of computer‑vision topics, delivered by leading researchers from the UK and abroad. The programme is designed for graduate students and early‑career researchers seeking hands‑on experience and exposure to current advances in the field.

name: Oxford Machine Learning Summer School 2026
venue: Oxford Machine Learning School, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: OxML 2026 is the Oxford Machine Learning School offering three advanced machine‑learning programmes in 2026. The programmes cover AI model building and agents (May 7‑8 & 15‑16), health and biomedical applications (July 10‑13), and representation learning with generative AI (July 15‑18), delivered online and in hybrid formats. The school targets researchers and practitioners seeking hands‑on experience with frontier AI technologies.

name: Robotics, Perception and Learning (RPL) Summer School
venue: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden
description: The RPL Summer School 2026 is a six‑day event organized by the Department for Robotics, Perception and Learning at KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm, Sweden. It brings together doctoral and postdoctoral researchers to discuss topics such as machine learning, computer vision, robotics, human‑robot interaction, planning and decision making through keynotes, industry talks, brainstorming sessions and student presentations. The program is hosted at the Happy Tammsvik resort, where participants receive fully funded accommodation, meals and activities, fostering collaboration and idea generation.

name: Machine Learning Crash Course at MALGA
description: The MLCC2026 Summer School – Machine Learning Crash Course – provides an introduction to fundamental machine‑learning concepts and algorithms. It is aimed at undergraduate and graduate students, as well as professionals, and is open to participants from any university after a selection process. The five‑day in‑person program in Genoa combines theoretical lectures with hands‑on lab sessions and includes a final test consisting of notebook work and a report.

name: UK Robotics Summer School
venue: National Robotarium, Heriot-Watt University, Edinburgh, Scotland, United Kingdom
description: The UK Robotics Summer School is a five‑day event held at the National Robotarium, Heriot‑Watt University in Edinburgh. It offers expert‑led lectures, tutorials, industry talks and hands‑on experience with state‑of‑the‑art robotics technology, targeting Master’s‑level students and industry practitioners. Participants can network with academics, peers, and industry leaders while enjoying refreshments, a special dinner, and exposure to cutting‑edge robotics challenges.

name: International Summer School for Advanced Studies on Biometrics, Behavior, and Vision
venue: Hotel Dei Pini, Porto Conte, Alghero, Sardinia, Italy
description: The 2027 Biometrics Summer School takes place at Hotel Dei Pini in Porto Conte near Alghero, Sardinia, Italy. It focuses on the impact of agentic AI and vision foundation models on biometrics and human recognition, covering topics such as machine learning, image understanding, signal analysis, neuroscience, robotics, and digital forensics. The program is aimed at PhD students, post‑docs, researchers, forensic examiners and professionals, offering intensive lectures, keynote talks, and optional videoconference participation with scholarships available.

name: Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal (ELS) aspects of AI and AS at Umeå University
description: The Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal aspects of AI and Autonomous Systems brings together researchers and practitioners at Umeå University in Sweden. It offers lectures, hands‑on multidisciplinary training, a poster session, and a social program to foster networking and professional exchange. The three‑day event (11–13 March 2026) targets students, faculty, and industry participants interested in responsible AI and autonomous systems.

name: Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM 2026)
description: The ACM Europe Winter School SoRAIM’27 focuses on social robotics, artificial intelligence, and multimedia. It targets PhD students and early‑career researchers, offering lectures, hands‑on sessions, and informal networking in a mountain setting. The program aims to foster cross‑disciplinary exchange among fields such as computer vision, speech processing, affective computing, and human‑robot interaction.

name: Northern Lights Deep Learning Winter School
venue: UiT The Arctic University of Norway, Tromsø, Norway
description: The 2027 NLDL Winter School is part of the Northern Lights Deep Learning Conference and will be held in Tromsø, Norway. It runs from 11 to 15 January and offers intensive lectures and workshops on state‑of‑the‑art deep‑learning methods such as image classification, object detection, segmentation, time‑series prediction and speech recognition. The school is aimed at researchers and practitioners who want to exchange ideas, build collaborations and learn the latest advances in the field.

name: Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS)
description: The 7th Annual Nepal AI School is an 11‑day intensive in‑person program offering AI lectures, labs, and project work. It targets senior undergraduates, graduate students, PhD candidates, faculty, and industry professionals, covering topics such as geometric deep learning, generative modeling, neuro‑symbolic AI and more. The school aims to democratize AI research in South Asia by providing foundational training and fostering collaborations among local and international researchers.

name: EEML Summer School
description: The Eastern European Machine Learning Summer School takes place in Cetinje, Montenegro from 27 July to 1 August 2026. It offers a series of lectures and tutorials on modern machine‑learning research presented by experts from leading universities and industry labs across Europe and the United States. The program is aimed at graduate students, early‑career researchers, and professionals seeking intensive training and networking opportunities in the field.

name: Mediterranean Summer School
description: The Mediterranean Machine Learning (M2L) Summer School offers a focused five‑day program of keynotes, lectures, and practical sessions led by experienced AI experts. It is aimed at doctoral and outstanding master students, as well as academics and practitioners worldwide, with a particular emphasis on the Mediterranean region. The curriculum covers topics such as computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, reinforcement learning, and ethics, and includes networking opportunities like poster sessions and social activities.

name: AthNLP Summer School 2026
description: The Athens Natural Language Processing Summer School 2026 (AthNLP) is a week‑long intensive program focused on state‑of‑the‑art NLP research and applications. It is jointly organized by NCSR Demokritos, RC Athena, Athens University of Economics and Business, Heriot‑Watt University, Archimedes Unit/Athena RC, and ELLIS‑University of Manchester, and will be held on the NCSR Demokritos campus in Athens, Greece. The school also supports the 14th EETN Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SETN 2026) that follows immediately after the summer school.

name: Advanced Artificial Intelligence: GenAI & Deep Unsupervised Learning
venue: Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The Advanced Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning summer school at Lady Margaret Hall focuses on generative AI and deep unsupervised learning techniques. It is designed for STEM students with intermediate experience in AI/ML who want theoretical knowledge and hands‑on experience with real‑world applications. The programme is offered as a residential or online course, covering topics such as clustering, GANs, self‑supervised learning, and unsupervised reinforcement learning.

name: LUT Summer School
description: LUT Summer School is a one‑week academic event that offers intensive courses on sustainability, climate action, marketing, management, inventive thinking and the intersection of business and technology. The programme combines workshops, lectures, group work and a social programme, and is aimed at bachelor’s and master’s students from partner universities. Courses will be delivered on the Lappeenranta campus in August 2027, with a mix of online instruction and on‑site teaching.

name: 1st Internationa School on the Cognitive, Ethical, and Societal Dimensions of AI - AIces
description: AIces 2026 is the first International School on the Cognitive, Ethical and Societal Dimensions of Artificial Intelligence, held in Porto, Portugal. It is aimed at graduate and postgraduate students as well as industry practitioners who want multidisciplinary insight into AI foundations, challenges and risks. The programme features parallel courses, a symposium, open debates, and both face‑to‑face and live‑online participation, with recordings available for 45 days after the event.

name: Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI
venue: Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications, Rabat, Morocco
description: The 2nd edition AI Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI takes place at the Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications in Rabat, Morocco. It offers five days of theoretical lectures, hands‑on labs, and project work aimed at young researchers, Ph.D. students, post‑docs and industry professionals. Participants will learn state‑of‑the‑art AI techniques from world‑renowned experts and build a network of AI leaders in Morocco.

name: AI4Science Summer School
description: The 2nd Summer School on Advancing Scientific Discovery with AI is organized in Caen, Normandy, France, targeting the intersection of AI and scientific research. It offers hands‑on workshops and case studies covering machine learning for data analysis, AI‑driven experimental design, generative models, and integration with physical simulations, aimed at PhD students, post‑doctoral researchers, and scientists. The program emphasizes deep learning skills, requiring participants to have experience with Python, NumPy, and PyTorch, and provides resources for those needing to strengthen prerequisites.
